brute_force_culling_revived.detail.cull_: Removes entities that are not visible to the player in order to reduce rendering load.
Removes block entities that are hidden from view to improve performance.
brute_force_culling_revived.detail.tick_: Also skips the update logic of entities that are currently hidden, not just their rendering. This covers entities behind terrain as well as everything outside your field of view, so it saves a large amount of processor time when many entities are loaded. Mob sounds are unaffected, because those are sent by the server rather than produced locally. While skipped, entities stop spawning particles and their animations pause, both of which resume as soon as they come back into view. Entities within 16 blocks, glowing entities, ridden entities and anything on the skip lists always keep updating. Requires Entity Culling to be enabled.
brute_force_culling_revived.detail.cull_: Skips rendering chunks that are completely invisible to the player.
brute_force_culling_revived.detail.async: Uses a separate thread to rebuild visible chunks asynchronously and then synchronizes them with the main rendering thread. This can improve frame rates during movement by speeding up chunk generation. Synchronization may cause short delays when rotating the camera quickly, which can make edge chunks load more slowly. You can increase the number of chunks processed in parallel in the game settings to help. This feature is experimental. If crashes occur while chunks are loading, disable this option.
brute_force_culling_revived.detail.sampl: Controls the scaling ratio of the depth texture used for culling. A higher ratio produces more accurate culling and better visual results. If performance is not affected, you can raise the ratio as much as possible. Avoid lowering it below 20 percent.
brute_force_culling_revived.detail.culli: Sets how many frames are delayed before the culling texture is updated on the CPU. This prevents incomplete data transmission from causing stuttering in the main thread. Higher values slow down culling speed. You can monitor update times for debugging. When shaders are enabled, data transmission slows down and the delay automatically increases by one frame.
brute_force_culling_revived.detail.bench: Runs an automated A/B performance test. Spawns 400 AI-less zombies in a ring around you, seals you inside a stone shell and surrounds it with 150 chests, then alternates three rounds of four seconds without culling and four seconds with culling, panning the camera at a realistic speed. Both sides of a round trace the same arc so they see an identical scene, and each round advances to the next arc, so the three rounds together sweep the full circle. The pan is deliberately slow: block entities are only registered for culling while their chunk section is already in the frustum, so spinning quickly never lets them settle on a verdict and under-reports that path. Alternating the two sides keeps clock drift and thermal throttling from landing on whichever side runs last. Vsync and the framerate limit are disabled for the run and restored afterwards, along with the blocks, the mobs, your camera angle and the debug level. Do not move while it runs; moving more than two blocks aborts it. Results report median and average frame time, 1% and 0.1% lows, the round-to-round spread, and culled counts. Entity and block entity counts are measured in view, after vanilla frustum culling, so they are far lower than the number spawned.
brute_force_culling_revived.detail.check: Testing option that allows you to check depth and culling texture functionality when the monitoring panel is open.
brute_force_culling_revived.detail.debug: Testing option that inverts the culling result, so the world draws only what culling removed. Anything you can still see is being culled wrongly. It applies to entities and block entities, and to chunks as well when Sodium or Embeddium is installed. While it is enabled the depth and culling maps stop updating, so the result is a snapshot taken the moment you switched it on: stand still while reading it, and switch it off before moving on.
brute_force_culling_revived.detail.nvidi: Warning: Not compatible with Nvidium’s asynchronous BFS feature.
brute_force_culling_revived.detail.auto_: On some devices, using shaders together with asynchronous chunk building can cause crashes. This setting automatically disables asynchronous chunk building when shaders are active.
brute_force_culling_revived.detail.sodiu: Warning: Requires Sodium or Embeddium to function.
brute_force_culling_revived.skip_culling: Block entities are excluded from culling
